ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R6-CP-03: Unbounded dust accumulation via _splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight (FixedHelper.sol:1706-1708)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test executes 50 alternating output-based swaps and verifies reserves+fees <= actual token balances. Solvency invariant holds — dust is bounded per-swap and aggregate dust does not cause reserve inflation.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R6-CP-04: Fee path divergence on partial fill fallback (FixedHelper.sol:915)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test performs input-based swaps and verifies solvency. The output-path fee denominator (MAX_BPS - poolFeeBPS) produces slightly higher fees than the input path, but this favors the protocol (LPs), not the attacker. No extraction path for attacker.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R6-CP-05: Both addInRange conservative revert at line 349 uses originalAdd0
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test attempts addLiquidity with both addInRange0=true and addInRange1=true. The operation either succeeds or reverts conservatively — the check at line 349 is overly strict but only blocks legitimate deposits, not enabling extraction. DoS requires self-inflicted parameter choice.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R6-CP-06: Protocol fee validation rounding divergence (AMMModule.sol:1667)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test executes 40 small swaps alternating direction and verifies reserves+fees <= actual balances. Rounding in _validateProtocolFees always favors protocol safety. No insolvency path.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R6-CP-07: Precision truncation over-withdrawal at lines 360-363 of FixedHelper
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test withdraws 1 unit from position after swaps. With spacing=1 (standard config), truncation loss is 0. With higher spacing (MAX=24), truncation bounded by spacing-1. Over-withdrawal limited to 23 wei max — dust level, not economically exploitable.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R6-CP-08: Dynamic fee hook at 100% BPS (AMMModule.sol:1717)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pure Forge test confirms: 10000 BPS blocked by guard (poolFeeBPS >= MAX_BPS). 9999 BPS (99.99%) passes by design — users choose to swap in hook-controlled pools. Self-inflicted config, not a vulnerability.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R6-CP-09: Fee burn at zero liquidity heights (FixedHelper.sol:1912-1926)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test removes all liquidity then attempts swap — swap correctly reverts with no liquidity. Solvency maintained. Fee burn at zero-liquidity heights is by design (no LP to claim). Not exploitable since attacker cannot create zero-liquidity heights with other people's positions.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R6-CP-01: snapPrice off-by-one at DynamicHelper.sol:264 (next == targetTick)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test in dynamic pool repo covers snapPrice boundary condition at exact initialized tick. The check 'next > targetTick' for downward movement correctly allows snapping TO an initialized tick boundary. The subsequent swap will cross that tick normally and activate liquidity as expected. No price manipulation vector found.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R6-CP-02: SingleProvider DoS band on partial fill fallback (SingleProviderHelper.sol:43-49)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge tests in single-provider repo verify fee path bounded behavior and round-trip loss. The narrow DoS band (1-2 wei boundary) requires oracle manipulation to hit precisely, and even then only causes swap revert (griefing), not extraction. User can retry with slightly different amount.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R6-CP-10: Withdrawal exceeds requested due to precision truncation (FixedHelper.sol:74)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Covered by CP-07 test. The withdraw0 = value0 - redeposited0 formula correctly handles precision alignment. With MAX_HEIGHT_SPACING=24, maximum over-withdrawal is 23 wei — dust level. The user requesting withdrawal of 1 gets at most 24 instead of 1, which is bounded and not economically exploitable.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C23: No profitable round-trip (INV-SW02)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test: swap USDC->WETH then WETH->USDC. Bob's final USDC balance <= initial. Fees eat into position. Round-trip invariant holds.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C24: Sequential small swaps protocol never loses (INV-SW03)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test: 100 small sequential swaps (50 per direction). Reserves + fees never exceed actual token balances. Protocol solvency maintained.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C3: _splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight — 1 wei and large swap edge cases
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge tests with 1 wei input and 10,000 USDC input. Solvency holds in both cases. No value creation from edge-case amounts.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C5: swapByOutput — full reserve and zero amount edge cases
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge tests: full reserve output request correctly fills or reverts; zero amount request correctly reverts. No free tokens.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C6: Add then remove liquidity round-trip rounding loss
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test: add 10,000 USDC then withdrawAll. Difference between deposit and withdrawal <= 2 wei. Rounding loss is dust-level.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C17: Fee calculations at edge BPS values (0, 1, 9999)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pure Forge tests: 0 BPS = 0 fee, 1 BPS = correct minimal fee, 9999 BPS = 99.99% fee. All calculations correct via FullMath.mulDivRoundingUp.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C25: Fee monotonicity across 20 alternating swaps
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test: feeBalance0 and feeBalance1 are monotonically non-decreasing across 20 swaps. Fees never decrease.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C26: Cetus-pattern precision extraction via extreme sqrtPriceX96
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pure Forge test: normalizePriceToRatio(type(uint160).max) and normalizePriceToRatio(1) both produce nonzero ratios. No overflow-to-zero path.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C27: Balancer rounding direction — 200 sequential 1-wei swaps
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test: 100 pairs of 1-wei swaps in each direction. AMM USDC and WETH balances never decrease. Rounding favors protocol.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C28: First depositor inflation (ERC-4626 pattern)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test: first LP deposits 100 units, second LP deposits 10,000e6. Both succeed. FixedPoolType uses direct amounts, not shares — ERC-4626 inflation attack is not applicable.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C29: Hook price manipulation — extreme ratio swap
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test: pool created with 1000x normal price ratio. Swap attempt either succeeds with solvency maintained or correctly reverts. No overflow or free tokens from extreme prices.

theft_theses.thesis: Exploit unbounded dust accumulation in FixedHelper._splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight to drain pool reserves via many small output-based swaps
Exploit fee path divergence on partial fill to systematically overcharge swappers and extract LP profit
Exploit snapPrice off-by-one to manipulate which liquidity activates at attacker-chosen price
Exploit precision truncation in withdrawal to withdraw more than requested

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If attacker snaps price to exact initialized tick boundary where next==targetTick, the strict > check at line 264 allows it through, and the snap sets price at an initialized tick. But the subsequent swap crosses that tick normally, activating liquidity as designed.
hypothesis_results.detail: The strict > check at line 264 is correct. When next==targetTick, the loop breaks at line 274 (next <= targetTick), and price is set at line 289. The tick crossing happens on the next swap, which is the expected behavior. No manipulation vector.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If attacker manipulates hook oracle to set price in the 1-wei DoS band where amountOut barely exceeds reserveOut, the fallback path reverts due to higher amountIn from output fee formula. But this only causes swap revert (griefing), requiring oracle control and producing no extraction.
hypothesis_results.detail: The revert at line 49 is a safety guard preventing the user from paying more than their input. The DoS band is 1-2 wei wide, requires oracle manipulation, and only causes revert (user can retry). No extraction path exists.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If an attacker executes 1000 output-based swaps producing 1 unit dust each, total accumulated dust reaches ~1000 units. When an LP withdraws, they receive position value + all dust, potentially exceeding pool reserves.
hypothesis_results.detail: Dust is bounded per-swap by potentialDustForOneInput check at line 1699. After 50 alternating output-based swaps, reserves+fees still <= actual token balances. The dust accumulation is absorbed by rounding surplus in the reserves (output rounding favors protocol). No insolvency detected.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If a partial fill fallback triggers at line 915, the output-path fee formula uses denominator MAX_BPS-poolFeeBPS (smaller), producing ~0.01% higher fees. Over many such swaps, this systematically overcharges swappers.
hypothesis_results.detail: The higher fee on the output path is by design — it compensates for the different fee calculation methodology. The overcharge benefits LPs (protocol-favorable rounding). An attacker cannot extract from this because the fee difference goes to LPs, not to a specific party the attacker controls.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If an LP sets both addInRange0=true and addInRange1=true with crafted amounts where depth1ValueOf0 > originalAdd0 but < originalAdd0+depth0, the overly conservative check at line 349 reverts the transaction when it could succeed.
hypothesis_results.detail: The conservative check at line 349 may block some legitimate dual-addInRange deposits, but this is a self-inflicted parameter issue (LP chooses the flags). The check prevents underflow, not a vulnerability. No extraction path — the worst case is a reverted add-liquidity transaction.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If the proportional fee adjustment at AMMModule:1415 rounds UP while the pool type's actual protocol fee rounds DOWN, the validation at line 1671 reverts legitimate swaps during partial fills.
hypothesis_results.detail: The fallback at line 1667 uses expectedProtocolLPFee when totalFees < expectedLPFee, which is a safety measure. After 40 small swaps, solvency holds — reserves+fees never exceed actual balances. The rounding divergence, if it occurs, causes revert (DoS for specific edge-case amounts), not extraction.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If FixedHelper truncates endHeight computation at lines 360-363 with large spacing (max=24), withdrawing 1 token could round up to withdraw an entire spacing-worth of tokens (up to 23 extra wei).
hypothesis_results.detail: MAX_HEIGHT_SPACING is capped at 24 (Constants.sol:23). Maximum over-withdrawal is 23 wei — dust level. Tested with spacing=1 (standard): no over-withdrawal detected. Even with maximum spacing, the extra 23 wei per withdrawal operation is not economically exploitable (gas cost to execute vastly exceeds the gain).

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If a malicious hook returns poolFeeBPS=10000 for an input swap, the AMM guard at line 1717 checks (true && 10000>10000) || (10000>=10000) = TRUE, correctly reverting. For 9999 BPS, the check passes — 99.99% fee allowed.
hypothesis_results.detail: Pure logic test confirms: 10000 BPS correctly blocked. 9999 BPS (99.99%) allowed by design. Users choose to swap in hook-controlled pools. The hook creator sets the fee — this is not a vulnerability but an intentional design choice. Pool with malicious fees is a self-inflicted config error.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If fees are distributed to heights with zero liquidity (lines 1912-1926), those fees are effectively burned — deducted from feeAmount but never credited to feeGrowthGlobal. An attacker could create zero-liquidity heights to burn other LPs' fees.
hypothesis_results.detail: Tested: after removing all liquidity, swap correctly reverts with no liquidity. An attacker cannot create zero-liquidity heights in OTHER people's positions. Fee burn at zero-liquidity is a consequence of LP withdrawal, not an attack vector. The burned fees came from the LP's own position.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If precision truncation at lines 360-363 causes redeposited0 to be much less than (value0 - requested_amount0), the withdraw0 = value0 - redeposited0 would return more tokens than the user requested.
hypothesis_results.detail: Same as CP-07. The truncation is bounded by MAX_HEIGHT_SPACING-1 = 23 wei. Tested with minimal withdrawal request (1 unit) after swaps — no over-withdrawal detected with spacing=1. Not economically exploitable.
